acceptance.reason: both administrator steps are applied and verified: the VS Installer background download is closed (policy keys set, scheduled task Disabled, no download process running) and the crash capture switch is open (CrashDumpEnabled=2, AutoReboot=0, AlwaysKeepMemoryDump=1, MinidumpsCount=20, DumpLogLevel=3) with the crash watch metrics collector actively writing CSV. The C: page file is pinned to an explicit size, but the new size only takes effect after one reboot, so the first kernel dump still needs that reboot.

authority: read-only status measurement; nothing written, nothing disabled, no transaction sent

crashForensics.note: The capture switch is measured, not assumed: CrashDumpEnabled=2 (kernel memory dump), AutoReboot=0 (keep the scene), AlwaysKeepMemoryDump=1, MinidumpsCount=20, DumpLogLevel=3. The C: page file is pinned to an explicit 32768/32768 MB because a kernel dump needs a system drive page file at least as large as physical memory, and it used to be system managed as 0 0 while the real backing store sat on E:. The pinned size only takes effect after one reboot, so until then the running allocation is still the old value and the first kernel dump needs that reboot.

directTrigger.note: closing the background download lowers the crash frequency but does not remove the crash itself. The capture switch and the fixed C: page file are what turn the next failure into something analysable.
directTrigger.what: the CPU level WHEA hardware error

sandboxMitigation.note: the watchdog kills a running download process without elevation, but it cannot stop the scheduled task from starting the next one
